title: Mandarin phoneme backend capability acceptance
hypothesis: A 26-phoneme Mandarin source-filter backend driven only by phone ids, F0 curve, timing and a voice template renders every advertised phoneme plus multi-phoneme sequences with <=1% median F0 error, a measurable voiced/unvoiced contrast (autocorrelation peak >0.85 for vowels/nasals/laterals, <0.30 for fricatives), template-dependent formant positions, and bit-identical CPU/MPS tensor hand-off, without copying any real-recording waveform.

errata: E1: the probe was written and run before this README was filled in, so criteria C1-C6 existed only in probe/test code at run time; the README records them after the fact.

E2: the pre_band_fix noise mask was a bump at the lower band edge rather than a band-pass, so /s/ stopped at 6.4 kHz and /sh/ lost everything above 2.7 kHz. Found by EXP-0010, fixed in src/vhe/synth/mandarin.py::_noise.

E3: after the fix /f/ still carries 22% of its energy in 8-12 kHz and has a higher spectral centroid (6156 Hz) than /sh/ (5051 Hz). Bands are hand-set placeholders awaiting real fricative spectra; not tuned away here.

E4: estimate_f0 locks onto a high harmonic for /a/ at 210 Hz (842 Hz) and 300 Hz (902 Hz) with the default 65-900 Hz search range; the probe avoids this with fmax_hz=1.5*f0, which a real pipeline cannot do. Cross-recorded in EXP-0011.
